findings.reason: the §9 inventory and its done-when must name and detect all four `serve.py` sites (or replace the grep with an AST pass over `.replace` calls), or the section ships with two forks outstanding and a green completion check.
findings.text: §9 lists `serve.py` as carrying two write-then-replace sites, but the module carries four: `_client_asset` (:498-503) and `compile_jsx` (:562-567) also publish through a sibling temporary and `temporary.replace(destination)`, a form §9's done-when grep `os.replace(|.replace(path)|with_suffix(".tmp")|.tmp` cannot match because the destination variable is neither named `path` nor carries a `.tmp` suffix. The section's own completion test therefore passes while these two duplicates of the `reckon/_store.py` owner remain, repeating at one level down the exact defect — a rename hidden inside a helper, invisible to a call-site counter — that §8 was created to fix; the repository already owns AST instruments (`docs/research` census, `reckon/clones.py`) that a `.replace` pass would use instead of the grep.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §8 promotes one primitive whose interface (`path, render, *, fsync, mode, fsync_directory`) is far smaller than what it hides (unique sibling creation, umask-correct mode via create-then-chmod, cleanup on any failure, file fsync, rename, optional directory fsync), and §9 routes the package's forks through that one interface with each site's payload as the render callback; the two public entry points add serialization behaviour rather than forwarding.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §9's inventory names `serve.py` as carrying two write-then-replace sites and judges completion with a grep that cannot see the `temporary.replace(destination)` form, so two further atomic-publish forks in `reckon/serve.py` survive the section whose purpose is to remove them.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1474, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §8 adds exactly one public definition and states in its own text that it retires the underscore-private forks (uncounted, so the family cannot shrink), §9 adds none and says so, and §7 changes only the expression of an existing constant and adds no definition. No section adds surface without accounting for it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the three sections landing next each name the mechanism they extend rather than proposing new machinery: §7 cites the exact site and expression (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:3844`, `5 * REVIEW_MAX_SCORE * 9 // 10`), §8 names the owner primitive it promotes (`reckon/_store.py:419 _write_through_sibling_temporary`) and every fork beside it, and §9 inventories the package-wide forks and the one owner they migrate onto.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no section adds a forwarding layer: §8 promotes an already-existing private primitive and §9 deletes the private helper around each migrated site, so what is proposed is extension of the owner, not a parallel thin layer.
